title: Multi-fold Origami is Algebraically Complete
description: Proves that multi-fold origami is algebraically complete: every polynomial degree d > 0 is k-fold constructible for some finite k. The j-th prime (0-indexed) requires exactly j folds — it is j-fold constructible but not (j-1)-fold constructible — establishing that the strict hierarchy of fold levels is infinite.

overview.historicalContext: The classical angle trisection impossibility (Wantzel, 1837) was overcome by origami: Huzita-Hatori axioms enable construction of cube roots. Alperin (2000) and Alperin-Lang (2006) showed that 1-fold origami corresponds to 3-smooth polynomial degrees and 2-fold to 5-smooth degrees. The natural extension — $k$-fold origami corresponds to $p_k$-smooth degrees — was formalized in AngleTrisectionOQ05OQ01. This file answers the next question: does allowing more folds eventually reach all polynomial degrees? Yes — multi-fold origami is algebraically complete.
overview.problemStatement: Is multi-fold origami algebraically complete for polynomial equations? That is, for every polynomial degree $d > 0$, does there exist a finite fold level $k$ such that $d$ is $k$-fold constructible?
overview.text: Proves algebraic completeness of multi-fold origami: every degree d > 0 is k-fold constructible for k = d. Identifies the exact fold level for each prime: the j-th prime (0-indexed) requires exactly j folds. Shows the strict hierarchy is infinite: for any K, the (K+1)-th prime requires > K folds.
overview.proofStrategy: Three main ingredients: (1) Nat.nth_mem_of_infinite gives primality of foldPrimeBound j. (2) Strict monotonicity (nth_strictMono) gives foldPrimeBound k < foldPrimeBound j when k < j, so the j-th prime's self-divisibility witnesses non-constructibility below fold j. (3) Algebraic completeness wraps eventually_constructible from the parent file.
keyInsights: The j-th prime (foldPrimeBound j) has exactly one prime factor — itself — so constructibility at level k reduces to the single inequality: foldPrimeBound j ≤ foldPrimeBound k, i.e., j ≤ k by strict monotonicity
This gives a perfect bijection between primes and minimum fold levels: p_j ↔ fold level j, revealing the prime sequence as the 'complexity ladder' for origami
Algebraic completeness (every degree is eventually constructible) follows from eventually_constructible in the parent file, with witness k = d using Nat.add_two_le_nth_prime
The strict hierarchy being infinite (min_folds_unbounded) follows from the infinitude of primes: each prime p_{K+1} is a new 'hard' degree requiring > K folds
prerequisites: Prime number theory: infinitude, divisibility, Nat.nth enumeration

sections.title: Primality of Fold Prime Bounds
sections.summary: Proves foldPrimeBound j = Nat.nth Nat.Prime j is prime for all j, using Nat.nth_mem_of_infinite Nat.infinite_setOf_prime.
sections.mathContext: $\text{foldPrimeBound}(j) = p_j$ is the $j$-th prime (0-indexed). Primality follows directly from $p_j \in \{n \mid \text{Nat.Prime}(n)\}$ via Mathlib's `Nat.nth\_mem\_of\_infinite`.

sections.title: Not Constructible Below the j-th Fold Level
sections.summary: Proves the j-th prime is NOT k-fold constructible for k < j (k ≥ 1). Key step: since foldPrimeBound j is prime and divides itself, smoothness at level k would require foldPrimeBound j ≤ foldPrimeBound k, contradicting foldPrimeBound k < foldPrimeBound j from nth_strictMono.
sections.mathContext: If $p_j$ were $k$-fold constructible with $k < j$, then IsSmooth$(p_k, p_j)$ would force $p_j \leq p_k$. But $k < j$ gives $p_k < p_j$ by strict monotonicity. Contradiction.

sections.title: Constructible Exactly at the j-th Fold Level
sections.summary: Proves the j-th prime IS j-fold constructible (j ≥ 1): its only prime divisor is itself, so IsSmooth (foldPrimeBound j) (foldPrimeBound j) holds trivially. Combines with the previous theorem to give the exact fold level for j ≥ 2.
sections.mathContext: IsSmooth$(p_j, p_j)$: need all prime factors of $p_j$ to be $\leq p_j$. Since $p_j$ is prime, its only prime factor is itself, and $p_j \leq p_j$. Combined: $p_j$ requires fold level exactly $j$ (for $j \geq 2$).

sections.title: Main Theorem: Algebraic Completeness
sections.summary: Proves every degree d > 0 is k-fold constructible for some k ≥ 1. Directly wraps eventually_constructible from AngleTrisectionOQ05OQ01, where the witness is k = d.
sections.mathContext: For any $d > 0$: all prime factors $q$ of $d$ satisfy $q \leq d$ (divisibility bound), and $p_d = \text{foldPrimeBound}(d) \geq d+2 > d$ (Nat.add\_two\_le\_nth\_prime). So $d$ is $p_d$-smooth, hence $d$-fold constructible.

sections.title: Infinite Strict Hierarchy
sections.summary: Proves for any K there exists a degree requiring > K folds: the prime p_{K+1} is not k-fold constructible for any k ≤ K. Shows the strict fold hierarchy 1-fold ⊊ 2-fold ⊊ 3-fold ⊊ ··· is genuinely infinite.
sections.mathContext: The prime $p_{K+1}$ has no $k$-fold constructibility for $k \leq K$: it is $(K+1)$-fold constructible (by `nth_prime_constructible_at`) but not $k$-fold for $k \leq K$ (by `nth_prime_not_constructible_below`). The infinitude of primes guarantees this works for arbitrarily large $K$.

sections.title: Concrete Exact Fold Levels
sections.summary: Proves exact fold levels for 5 (exactly 2 folds), 7 (exactly 3 folds), 11 (exactly 4 folds), by instantiating prime_exact_fold_level at j=2,3,4 and applying fold_2_bound, fold_3_bound, fold_4_bound.
sections.mathContext: $p_2 = 5$ needs exactly 2 folds; $p_3 = 7$ needs exactly 3; $p_4 = 11$ needs exactly 4. These recover the strict hierarchy witnesses from the parent file via the general exact-fold-level theorem.

conclusion.summary: Proves multi-fold origami is algebraically complete: every polynomial degree is eventually constructible with enough folds. The j-th prime requires exactly j folds, giving a perfect bijection between the prime sequence and the 'difficulty ladder' of fold levels.
conclusion.implications: The algebraic completeness result means origami (with enough simultaneous folds) is as powerful as general algebra: it can realize any polynomial equation of any degree. The exact fold level theorem reveals that primes are the canonical 'hard' degrees — each prime p_j is the unique witness requiring exactly j folds. Together these results paint a complete picture: multi-fold origami transcends the classical ruler-and-compass hierarchy not by a fixed amount but by an unbounded progression, with primes marking each step.
openQuestions: Can the exact fold level theorem be extended to composite degrees: is there a simple formula for the minimum fold level of an arbitrary degree d in terms of its prime factorization?
The conjectured equivalence 'k-fold origami ↔ p_k-smooth degrees' (Alperin-Lang for k=1,2, open for k≥3): does algebraic completeness give any leverage on proving the conjecture for k≥3?
